props.name: indicatorSize
props.description: The size of the lane every `TimelineList.Item`'s indicator sits in: `dot` is 8.75px, `md` 24px and `lg` 32px. The status marks fill the lane, and at `md` and `lg` the complete and error marks carry a check and a cross. An Item without `status` keeps the 8.75px dot. In a vertical or alternate list the text moves down so a first line 22px tall centers on the mark. A `TimelineList.Title` has that line from level 3 down; a title at level 1 or 2 does not center on the mark. In a horizontal list the text sits under the rail, its start on the mark's start.

props.name: layout
props.description: The direction the list runs. `alternate` is a vertical list with the body and the `opposite` content on either side of the rail, swapped on every other `TimelineList.Item`. It folds to one side, the `opposite` content above the body, when the list is narrower than 32rem. It measures its own width, so give an alternate list a definite inline size, such as a block parent's width; in a parent that sizes to its content it has no width of its own. `horizontal` runs along the inline axis, with each `TimelineList.Item` at least 10rem wide. A horizontal list wider than its parent overflows and neither clips nor scrolls, so wrap it in `ScrollArea.Root` with `orientation="horizontal"`.

props.name: indicator
props.description: What shows in the lane. Unset, it shows the default mark for its `status`. `null`, `true`, `false` and `""` show nothing, and the line runs on to the Item's text. A node replaces the mark, centered in the lane, so pair it with an `indicatorSize` of `md` or `lg` on `TimelineList.Root`. The node is decorative and hidden from assistive technology, so keep its meaning in the text, and render no focusable control in it.

props.name: opposite
props.description: The content across the rail from the body, such as a `TimelineList.Time`. A vertical list then gives every `TimelineList.Item` a 7rem column before the rail, and a horizontal list puts the content above the rail. Below Chrome 117, which lacks row subgrid, a horizontal list shows it under the rail. `true`, `false` and `""` render no cell, so a condition such as `showDates && date` works. A `TimelineList.Time` among the children stays inline with the body.

props.name: status
props.description: The event's status, which draws its own mark. `current` sets `aria-current="step"` and adds no text. An `aria-current` the Item gets, `false` included, replaces it. `complete`, `upcoming` and `error` add visually hidden text before the children: "Completed", "Upcoming" or "Error" in the reader's locale. That text needs a `LocaleProvider` above the list. Unset, the lane shows the default dot and the content gains no text.

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: The visually hidden text that names the status, in place of the locale text. It also renders for `current`. An empty string renders no text. Not allowed without `status`.

props.name: font
props.description: The font weight. It replaces the medium weight every level sets.

props.name: level
props.description: The outline level, `1` to `6`, which picks the rendered `h1` to `h6`. The title keeps the same type in every theme: 24/33 at level 1, 18/24.75 at level 2 and 16/22 from level 3 down, all at 500, unless `size` or `font` replaces it.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: size
props.description: The type size. It replaces the size the `level` sets.

props.name: variant
props.description: The text color. `default` takes the color of the text around it, so text in an error message is the error color. The others set a text role. `brand` sets the brand color as text at 4.5:1 or more on the page and on a Card in every theme. On another surface, such as a filled panel or the Sidebar, check its contrast. To recolor brand text, override `--brand-ink`, not `--brand`, on the element that carries the theme attributes. Some themes declare `--brand-ink` as its own color, and a `--brand` override leaves that color unchanged.

props.name: date
props.description: The event's date or instant. An HTML date or date-time string passes through unchanged onto the host `dateTime`, so a server and a browser in different time zones render the same value. Such a string is a date, such as `2026-10-20`, or a date-time with an offset, such as `2026-10-20T10:00Z` or `2026-10-20T10:00+02:00`. A date-time without an offset names a different instant in each time zone, so development builds warn about one. The part normalizes a `Date` with `toISOString()`, and also any other string the JavaScript date parser reads, such as `June 15, 2024`, or `2024-02-30`, which the parser rolls over to March 1. An invalid value throws `RangeError("TimelineList.Time received an invalid date")`.
